doc_name: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
text: The Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) is a research university located in Masdar City, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates. Established in October 2019, it is the world's first graduate-level, research-based AI university and was founded as part of the UAE's Artificial Intelligence 2031 strategy, which aims to position the country as a global AI leader and includes the appointment of the world's first Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence. The university is named after Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, with its board of trustees chaired by Sultan Ahmed Al Jaber and its advisory board chaired by Omar Al Olama, the UAE's first Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence. The Ministry of Education accredited six graduate programs in February 2020 and granted the university a license in April 2020. The initial class of graduate students was scheduled to begin in the fall of 2020 but was delayed to January 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. When classes began, the university had 11 faculty members and 78 students (13 PhD and 65 MSc) in machine learning and computer vision, with the first classes held online using Moodle software; in-person classes started in the fall of 2021. The first cohort of PhD and MSc students graduated in January 2023. By 2024, at least 25 additional faculty members had been recruited, and departments in robotics, computer science, and statistics and data science were established. The first undergraduate program, a bachelor of science in artificial intelligence, launched in March 2025. MBZUAI's research program has four pillars: improving public and private sector services, enhancing industrial efficiency, supporting emerging high-value sectors, and optimizing environmental sustainability. It has a joint AI research program with the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel and a dedicated research hub on foundation models, coordinating the development of Jais, a large language model for Arabic, for Emirati government use. Other research hubs include the Center for Integrative Artificial Intelligence, the Metaverse Center, and the Institute of Digital Public Health, along with a business incubator and a joint lab with the Abu Dhabi Digital Authority. The university provides graduate students with a full scholarship package including a monthly stipend, health insurance, and accommodations in exchange for full-time commitment to AI study and research, designed to attract students from outside Western or Chinese AI hubs. As of 2025, the institution had 84 faculty members and over 200 postdocs and researchers. The 2024 intake included 209 students (147 MSc and 62 PhD) from 36 countries, with many being Chinese and 31% being women, and a student-faculty ratio of 5:1. By 2024, 212 students had graduated from master's and PhD programs, most of whom remain in the region. More than half pursue industry internships during their studies, and many participate in hackathons or research conferences. The university's goal is to produce a new generation of AI leaders and experts, and according to The Economist, it has recruited star professors from institutions such as the University of California, Berkeley, and Carnegie Mellon University. MBZUAI offers undergraduate, master's, and Ph.D. programs in artificial intelligence, computer science, computer vision, machine learning, natural language processing, robotics, and statistics & data science. The current president is Eric Xing, who joined in January 2021; Sir J. Michael Brady served as the founding, interim president, Professor Ling Shao was the founding provost and executive vice president, and Timothy Baldwin was appointed provost in April 2024. As of 2025, the Board of Trustees is chaired by Khaldoon Khalifa Al Mubarak. The campus is located in Masdar City, a sustainable urban community designed as a smart innovation cluster, and uses low-carbon transportation such as electric buses and golf carts. When classes began in 2021, the university had only six classrooms, most accommodating no more than 20 students; these were later redesigned to support remote and hybrid learning, including broadcasting lectures to multiple classrooms and online students. The campus also includes a gymnasium, swimming pool, and squash and badminton courts.
